slides.h1: Why Two Astrology Apps Give You Opposite Answers
slides.sub: Rule-based engine vs. synthesis engine — the difference, in plain terms.

slides.body: A long list of if-then rules. If Mars sits in the 7th house, flag it. Each rule fires on its own, with no awareness of the others.

points: Both get printed — you sort it out
More rules means more clashes, not more clarity

slides.body: It weighs layers together: the birth chart (D-1), Varga (divisional sub-charts for one life area), dasha (planetary period), gochar (current transits) and Ashtakavarga (bindu strength points).
Instead of printing both answers, it asks which layer governs this question and which timing window is live. A conflict becomes a ranked, explainable answer.

slides.h2: Where AI helps — and where it doesn't
slides.body: Weighing all these layers by hand is slow and error-prone. That is where AI earns its place. Judgement on the result still belongs to a trained astrologer.
